label: Q1

en: Correctly mentioned the shift from pastoral, semi‑nomadic Jana to settled Janapada/Mahajanapada states.
Accurately described the change from Sabha/Samiti assemblies to hereditary monarchies and the existence of Gana‑Sanghas like Vajji and Malla.
Noted the rigidification of the Varna system and the emergence of birth‑based Jatis.
hi: सही ढंग से बताया कि कैसे जटा (जाना) से स्थायी जनपद/महाजनपद राज्य बने।
सभा/समिति से वंशानुगत राजशाही और वैज्य‑मल्ला जैसे गण-संघों की ओर परिवर्तन को ठीक से उल्लेख किया।
वर्ण व्यवस्था के कठोर होने और जातियों के उभरने को सही रूप से बताया।

en: Inclusion of iron technology (PGW/NBPW) and its role in forest clearance, agricultural surplus and the second urbanisation.
Explanation of regular revenue systems (bhaga, bali, shulka) and the development of standing armies.
hi: लोहे की तकनीक (पीजीडब्ल्यू/एनबीपीडब्ल्यू) और उसके द्वारा वन कटाई, कृषि अधिकता तथा द्वितीय शहरीकरण में योगदान का उल्लेख नहीं किया।
भाग़ा, बलि, शुल्क जैसी नियमित कर प्रणाली और स्थायी सेना के गठन का विवरण नहीं दिया।

feedback.en: Well done on covering the main political and social transformations; add details on iron technology and fiscal‑military reforms for full marks.
feedback.hi: मुख्य राजनीतिक‑सामाजिक परिवर्तन को अच्छी तरह से बताया; पूर्ण अंक के लिए लोहे की तकनीक और कर‑सेना सुधारों का विवरण जोड़ें।

model_answer: The early Vedic community was a pastoral, semi‑nomadic tribe (jana) governed by clan assemblies (Sabha, Samiti). By the Mahajanapada era these tribes settled on fertile river plains, forming territorial agrarian states (janapada) with defined boundaries. Political power shifted from collective, lineage‑based councils to hereditary monarchs in most regions, while some areas (Vajji, Malla) developed oligarchic republics (gana‑sanghas). The varna system, originally occupational, became rigidly birth‑based, giving rise to numerous jatis that stratified society. The spread of iron tools (PGW/NBPW) cleared dense forests, boosted agricultural surplus and spurred a second urbanisation with towns and markets. Regular revenue systems—bhaga, bali and shulka—were instituted, and standing armies replaced the earlier voluntary tribal levies, consolidating state authority.
read_text: Transition from pastoral semi-nomadic tribal polity (Jana) to territorial agrarian states (Janapada/Mahajanapada) Shift from lineage-based Sabha/Samiti assemblies to hereditary monarchies and oligarchic republics (Gana-Sanghas like Vajji, Malla) Rigidification of Varna system from occupation-based (Early Vedic) to birth-based hierarchy and emergence of Jatis
